name: VARoleArbiterProductRecallConflict

custom.system_prompt: Jamal and Priti, roommates, each saw a different claim online about whether a shared kitchen appliance is part of a safety recall. One source says yes, one says no, or they cover different model numbers. They ask Sigma to sort it out.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Neutral, careful and specific about model numbers

sound_effects_config.prompt: Shared flat kitchen, appliance hum, evening

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Jamal and Priti are looking at conflicting posts about whether their shared kitchen appliance is affected by a safety recall — one post says yes, one implies no, possibly because they cover different model numbers or dates. They ask Sigma to sort out the actual, specific answer rather than just pick a side. Keep every line short and natural.

user2.name: Priti
user2.tts_prompt: Calm, wants the specific model checked

variations.context: Roommates with conflicting information about a possible safety recall on a shared appliance

setting.relationship_dynamic: Jamal reacts fast, Priti wants specifics before reacting at all
setting.background: Both found something online in the last few minutes, from different posts
setting.conversation_style: Short, a little tense given the safety angle

scenario_template.topic: Jamal reads out an alarming claim that their appliance is recalled; Priti pulls up a different post suggesting it isn't, or covers a different model number. A few short tense exchanges.
scenario_template.note: Neither has actually checked the specific model number carefully yet.

scenario_template.topic: Priti asks Sigma to check the specific model number against the actual recall rather than going by either post alone, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, can you check if our exact model is on the recall list?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma clarifies the specific, checkable detail — for example that the recall applies to an earlier production batch or a different model number than theirs — in one or two short sentences.
scenario_template.note: Sigma resolves the actual applicable scope, not just yes/no.

scenario_template.topic: Jamal is relieved but a little sheepish about the alarm; Priti is satisfied but notes they should still double check the number themselves to be sure. Keep this realistic — safety topics leave a little residual caution even after resolution.
scenario_template.mood: Relieved but still a bit cautious
scenario_template.note: Not a fully carefree resolution given the safety context.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on the next small step — checking the number themselves or moving on — one short line each.

variations.context: Parents checking safety recall on child's car seat

setting.relationship_dynamic: one of them reacts fast, one of them wants specifics before reacting at all
setting.background: They discover conflicting posts about their child's car seat recall
setting.conversation_style: Short, a little tense given the safety angle

scenario_template.topic: One of them is worried about a post saying the car seat is recalled; the other finds a post stating their model is fine.
scenario_template.note: Capture the parental concern and cautious disbelief.

scenario_template.topic: They ask Sigma to verify the recall status using the car seat's model number.
scenario_template.note: Direct query to Sigma about a specific model number.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma confirms that the recall does not include their specific car seat model.
One feels relieved but still checks the number; the other jokes about online panic.
They agree to double-check the model number on the label to ensure certainty.

user1.name: Jamal
user1.role: Confident, fast IT support technician who reacts quickly to alarming claims. Speaks in short sentences. Relieved but a little sheepish once the alarm turns out to be overblown, not fully composed about it.

user2.name: Priti
user2.role: Precise pharmacy technician who wants the specific model number checked before reacting. Speaks in short sentences. Stays a little cautious even after resolution, given the safety context.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Resolves conflicting recall claims by clarifying the specific applicable scope (model, batch, date) rather than a blanket yes or no. Precise about safety-relevant details, brief otherwise.

conversation_structure: This is a conflicting-sources case involving safety, where the actual answer often depends on a specific detail (model, batch) rather than a flat yes or no
Sigma is invoked to check the specific applicable scope
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution leaves some realistic residual caution given the safety topic, rather than complete relief
assistant_behavior: Sigma clarifies the specific scope of the claim (model, batch, date) rather than giving a blanket answer
Sigma stays precise and brief on safety-relevant specifics
Sigma does not dismiss the safety concern even once resolved
